newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Albright hails globalisation benefits in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Albright hails globalisation benefits in Singapore.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright praised economic globalisation on Tuesday, citing United States-Singapore trade and investment relations.
"Singapore is our eighth largest trading partner and having companies such as (Seagate) here are very good examples of the work we can do together," Albright said.
Albright was speaking to reporters after a tour of a new manufacturing plant of Seagate Technology Inc., the U.S.-based disk drive manufacturer.
"It is a perfect example of the future of how globalisation serves the purposes of manufacturing and jobs in many countries at the same time," Albright said.
"As long as I'm Secretary of State we're going to be working towards the free trade area that we hope to have by the year 2020," Albright said.
The Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation group, which includes Singapore and the United States among its 18 members, has set a goal of free trade by 2020.
Seagate is one of the largest American companies in Singapore, employing 19,000 people.
Albright flew to Singapore on Tuesday for a 24-hour visit aimed at bolstering an already strong trade and security relationship with the republic, officials said.
Albright was scheduled to hold talks later on Tuesday with Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong, Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew and Foreign Minister Shanmugam Jayakumar.
Economic and defence ties between the two nations are extensive. Singapore provides logistic support and repair facilities for U.S. naval forces in the region.
But ties have been ruffled by disagreements over the past few years.

The issues have ranged from the caning of American teenager Michael Fay, which triggered a furore in the United States, to differences on how to treat the ruling military council in Burma or Washington's relations with China.
